# Hypothetical Therapy Session: Client Statements

## Client Backstory

**Name:** Marcus Ellison, age 38
**Background:** Marcus is a former high school English teacher who left his teaching position 14 months ago after a prolonged period of burnout. He is married to his wife, Janelle (36), a pediatric nurse who works night shifts. They have two children: Aiden (7) and Mila (4). Marcus's mother, Dorothy, was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's disease two years ago and now lives in an assisted living facility 45 minutes away. His father, Raymond, passed away from a sudden heart attack when Marcus was 22, during his senior year of college, an event Marcus never fully processed. Marcus has one older brother, Dean (42), who lives in another state and rarely helps with their mother's care, which is a source of deep resentment. Marcus currently works part-time as a freelance copywriter from home but struggles with motivation and financial anxiety. He was diagnosed with major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder six months ago and has been on sertraline (Zoloft) 100mg for four months. He has been seeing his psychiatrist, Dr. Amara Osei, for three months. He played baseball in college and hasn't exercised regularly in over two years. He has a history of social withdrawal and has lost contact with most of his close friends. He occasionally drinks 3–5 beers in the evening to "quiet his mind." This is his seventh session.

---

## 100 Client Statements

### Opening / General State of Mind
1. "Honestly, Dr. Osei, this has been one of the harder weeks I've had in a while, and I wasn't sure I was even going to make it in today."

2. "I sat in the parking lot for about twenty minutes before I came in because I kept thinking, what's the point of talking about the same things over and over?"

3. "I know I'm supposed to say how I've been since last time, but I genuinely don't know how to summarize it — it's like everything blurs together."

4. "Some mornings I wake up and there's this heavy weight on my chest before I even open my eyes, like my body already knows the day is going to be too much."

5. "I feel like I'm living in slow motion while everyone around me is moving at normal speed."

6. "I've been going through the motions — feeding the kids, making coffee, sitting at my desk — but I don't feel like I'm actually present for any of it."

7. "Janelle asked me last night how I was doing and I just said 'fine,' and she gave me this look like she knows I'm lying but she's too tired to push."

### Depression Symptoms
8. "There are days when I don't shower until three in the afternoon, and only because I know Aiden's bus is coming and I have to stand outside."

9. "I used to love reading — I was an English teacher, for God's sake — and now I can't get through a single page without my mind going somewhere dark."

10. "I've started sleeping on the couch most nights, not because Janelle and I are fighting, but because I feel like I don't deserve to be in the bed next to her."

11. "Sometimes I'll be washing dishes and I just stop and stare out the window for I don't know how long — ten minutes, twenty — and then I snap out of it and feel like I lost time."

12. "I haven't felt joy — real, actual joy — in so long that I'm starting to wonder if I ever really did, or if I just imagined it."

13. "Last Saturday the kids were playing in the backyard and laughing, and I watched them from the kitchen and felt absolutely nothing, and that terrified me."

14. "I keep the blinds closed in my office all day. The sunlight feels like it's mocking me, if that makes any sense."

15. "I've lost about twelve pounds since I started coming here, and it's not on purpose — I just forget to eat, or food tastes like cardboard."

16. "I had a dream the other night that I was buried under wet sand and I could hear people walking above me, but no one was trying to dig me out."

17. "Everything feels gray. Not sad exactly, just… gray. Like someone turned the saturation down on my whole life."

18. "I used to make these elaborate lesson plans with creative projects for my students. Now I can barely write a 300-word product description without stalling out."

### Anxiety Symptoms
19. "My mind doesn't stop. Even when I'm exhausted, there's this constant ticker tape of worries running through my head — money, my mom, the kids, whether Janelle is going to leave me."

20. "I've been grinding my teeth so badly at night that I chipped a molar last week and I can't afford to get it fixed right now."

21. "I check my bank account probably six or seven times a day, even though I know the number isn't going to change."

22. "Sometimes my heart starts racing for no reason — I'll just be sitting at my desk and suddenly it feels like I've sprinted a mile."

23. "I've started making lists of everything that could go wrong, and I know it sounds crazy, but it feels like if I can anticipate the disaster, maybe I can survive it."

24. "I had a full-blown panic attack at the grocery store last Wednesday — I had to leave the cart in the aisle and sit in my car with the air conditioning on full blast."

25. "I keep replaying conversations in my head, analyzing every word I said, convinced I sounded stupid or that people are judging me."

26. "The thought of answering the phone makes my stomach drop. I've let calls from my mom's facility go to voicemail three times this week."

27. "I catastrophize everything. Aiden had a cough on Monday and within an hour I'd convinced myself it was something serious and I'd Googled every worst-case scenario."

28. "My hands shake sometimes when I'm trying to type, and I can't tell if it's the anxiety or the medication."

29. "I wake up at 3 a.m. almost every night with this surge of dread, like something terrible is about to happen but I can't figure out what it is."

30. "I've started avoiding the mailbox because I'm terrified there's going to be a bill in there that we can't pay."

### Relationship with Wife (Janelle)
31. "Janelle and I barely talk anymore — and when we do, it's logistics. Who's picking up Aiden. Whether we paid the electric bill. Nothing real."

32. "She works the night shift three or four days a week, and honestly, part of me is relieved when she's gone because I don't have to pretend I'm okay."

33. "I can see the frustration in her eyes. She married a guy who had ambitions, who coached little league, who made her laugh — and now she's got this hollow version of me."

34. "We haven't been intimate in over three months, and I know some of that is the medication, but it's more than that — I feel like I have nothing to offer her."

35. "She suggested couples counseling last month and I shut it down immediately, which I know wasn't fair, but the idea of sitting in another room explaining how broken I am was just too much."

36. "Last week she said, 'Marcus, I need you to be here — really here — because I can't do this alone,' and I couldn't even look at her."

37. "Sometimes I think she'd be better off without me, and that's not me being dramatic — I genuinely believe the math works out better for her if I'm not in the equation."

38. "I found her crying in the laundry room on Sunday. She didn't know I saw her. I just walked away because I didn't know what to say."

39. "She's carrying everything — her job, the kids, the house, my mom's insurance paperwork — and I feel like dead weight."

### Children (Aiden, 7, and Mila, 4)
40. "Aiden asked me last week why I don't play catch with him anymore, and I made up some excuse about my shoulder hurting, but the truth is I just didn't have the energy."

41. "I snapped at Mila on Thursday for spilling juice on my laptop, and the look on her face — I can still see it. She's four. She didn't deserve that."

42. "I'm scared that they're going to grow up and remember me as the dad who was always in his room with the door closed."

43. "Aiden's teacher sent home a note saying he's been more withdrawn in class, and I can't shake the feeling that he's absorbing my depression somehow."

44. "Mila crawled into my lap yesterday and said, 'Daddy, are you sad?' and I almost lost it right there."

45. "I missed Aiden's baseball game two weekends ago. I told Janelle I had a deadline, but I was just lying on the couch staring at the ceiling."

46. "I love my kids more than anything, but sometimes being around their energy is physically exhausting, and then I hate myself for feeling that way."

47. "I keep thinking about my own dad and how present he was before he died, and I'm here, alive, and I can't even be half the father he was."

### Mother's Illness (Dorothy / Alzheimer's)
48. "I visited my mom on Saturday and she didn't recognize me for the first ten minutes. She kept calling me Raymond — my dad's name."

49. "The facility called to say they're raising the monthly rate by $400, and I have no idea where that money is going to come from."

50. "Watching her disappear piece by piece is the cruelest thing I've ever experienced. Some days she's almost herself, and those days are almost worse because I know they won't last."

51. "I feel guilty every single day that I'm not there more. I go once a week, sometimes every two weeks if it's bad, and that's not enough."

52. "She was a sharp woman — she did the New York Times crossword in pen every morning — and now she can't remember the word for 'window.'"

53. "Sometimes I drive to the facility and sit in the parking lot and can't go in. I'll sit there for thirty minutes and then drive home."

54. "The staff keeps asking me about her advance directives and long-term care plans, and every time they bring it up I feel like I'm going to pass out."

55. "I'm grieving someone who's still alive, and nobody tells you how to do that."

### Brother (Dean)
56. "Dean called last week — first time in two months — and had the audacity to ask how Mom was doing like he's been involved at all."

57. "He lives in Charlotte, which is five hours away, and he acts like that's the same as being on another planet. He's visited Mom twice in the past year."

58. "I told him I needed help with the facility costs and he said he'd 'see what he could do,' which is his way of saying no."

59. "Part of me wants to scream at him, and part of me is jealous that he can just… not carry this. He just opts out and nobody holds him accountable."

60. "We used to be close. After Dad died, we kind of drifted, and now it feels like we're strangers who happen to share a last name."

61. "He told me at Thanksgiving that I 'take things too personally' and that I 'chose' to handle Mom's care. Like it was some kind of hobby I picked up."

### Father's Death (Raymond)
62. "I never really dealt with my dad's death. I was 22, in my last semester of college, and I just pushed through. Graduated, got a job, kept moving."

63. "He dropped dead of a heart attack at 56 while mowing the lawn. No warning. No goodbye. I found out from a phone call while I was in the campus library."

64. "I think about him every single day, and it's been sixteen years. Is that normal? Does grief have an expiration date?"

65. "He would have known what to do about Mom. He always knew what to do. I don't have that — I don't have that certainty about anything."

66. "Sometimes I worry that I'm going to die the same way — suddenly, without getting to say the things I need to say — and that thought keeps me up at night."

67. "I was angry at him for a long time. Angry that he didn't take better care of himself. Angry that he left us. I know that's irrational, but the feeling is still there."

### Career / Work / Identity
68. "I left teaching because I was burning out, but now I don't even know who I am without it. My identity was 'Mr. Ellison, the English teacher,' and now I'm just… nothing."

69. "Freelancing sounded like freedom, but it's really just isolation with a laptop and no structure."

70. "I had a client email me for a revision last week and I couldn't bring myself to open it for three days. I just stared at the notification."

71. "I made $1,400 last month. That's it. Janelle's salary covers most of the bills, but I can see the resentment building even though she'd never say it outright."

72. "I used to dream about writing a novel. I had notebooks full of ideas. Now those notebooks are in a box in the garage and I can't even look at them."

73. "My old principal emailed me asking if I'd consider coming back for the fall semester, and I didn't respond because the thought of standing in front of a classroom again makes me nauseous."

74. "I feel like a failure. I'm 38 years old, barely employed, and my wife is the one holding everything together."

75. "Some days I sit at my desk for six hours and produce nothing. Not a single sentence. And then the guilt eats me alive."

### Social Isolation
76. "My best friend from college, Terrence, has called me probably a dozen times in the last few months and I haven't picked up once."

77. "I deleted most of my social media because seeing other people's lives — their vacations, their promotions — made me feel physically sick."

78. "I used to be part of a Wednesday night poker group with guys from the school. I stopped going eight months ago and eventually they stopped inviting me."

79. "I don't even know how to have a normal conversation anymore. The few times I've been around other people, I feel like I'm performing."

80. "Janelle's sister had a birthday party for her kids and I told Janelle to take Aiden and Mila without me. I said I had work. I didn't have work."

81. "I feel like I've built this invisible wall around myself and now I don't know how to take it down, even when I want to."

### Medication / Treatment
82. "The Zoloft is taking the edge off the very worst of it, I think, but it also makes me feel kind of flat, like I can't access any emotions — good or bad."

83. "I've gained a weird tolerance for the numbness. At first it scared me, but now it almost feels safer than actually feeling things."

84. "The sexual side effects are a real problem. I haven't said anything to Janelle about it, but it's another thing that makes me feel broken."

85. "I missed two days of my medication last week — not on purpose, I just forgot — and by the second day I felt these electric zap feelings in my head."

86. "Is it normal that I still have bad days even on the medication? Because I thought it was supposed to fix this."

87. "Sometimes I wonder if I should be on something stronger, or something different, or if medication is even the right path at all."

88. "I've been reading about people who've been on antidepressants for years and never come off, and that scares me."

### Alcohol Use
89. "I've been having a few beers most nights after the kids go to bed. It's the only time my brain actually quiets down."

90. "Janelle found the recycling full of cans on Tuesday and didn't say anything, but I saw her counting them."

91. "I know I shouldn't be drinking on the Zoloft. I read the label. But at 10 p.m. when I can't stop thinking, a beer feels more effective than a breathing exercise."

92. "It's never been hard liquor, and I never drink during the day, so I keep telling myself it's not a problem. But I know that's the kind of thing people with a problem say."

93. "My dad used to have a beer on the porch after work every night. I tell myself I'm just doing what he did, but he had one. I'm having four or five."

### Self-Worth / Existential Thoughts
94. "I don't think about hurting myself, not exactly, but sometimes I think about what it would be like if I just… wasn't here. Like if I could press pause on existing."

95. "I keep asking myself when I became this person. I look in the mirror and I don't recognize the guy staring back at me."

96. "I feel like I'm disappointing every single person in my life — Janelle, my kids, my mom, even you, Dr. Osei — and I don't know how to stop the spiral."

97. "There's this voice in my head that says I'm weak for needing help, that real men just handle their problems. I know that's not true, but the voice is loud."

98. "I had this thought the other day that maybe I peaked at 28 — good job, healthy relationship, Dad was still alive — and everything since has been a slow downhill slide."

99. "I want to get better. I really do. I just don't know if I believe I can anymore, and that might be the scariest part of all of this."

100. "Thank you for not giving up on me, Dr. Osei. I know I cancel sometimes, and I know I deflect, and I know I'm not the easiest patient — but this room is one of the few places where I feel like it's okay to not be okay."
